# 1101 — SECURITY: dot-segment traversal defeats the redirect allowlist's path boundary

Build-start snapshot (batch order #1 of 6: 1101 → 1102 → 1098 → 1103 → 1100 → 1099).
Full approved plan + challenge dispositions live on maestro Inbox item 1101.

## Objective
Fail-closed refusal of any URL whose PATH carries a `.`/`..` segment (any `%2e` spelling),
via one `_has_dot_segment` guard in `redirect_allowlist._split`, placed ahead of the scheme
branch so it covers http(s) and custom-scheme URLs alike. Refuse, do not normalize.

## Load-bearing build instructions (from the two red-team reviews)
- The guard runs on `parts.path` ONLY, never the raw URL (tab/newline bypass + query-match break otherwise).
- `_PCT_DOT = re.compile(r"%2e", re.IGNORECASE)`, decode-then-split-on-`/`, equality test vs `(".","..")`.
- Do NOT decode `%252e` or `%2f` (a browser resolves neither).
- Insert in `_split` after the `urlsplit` try/except, before `scheme = ...`.
- Optional hardening: in `report_unlisted_destination`, fall back to `urlsplit(destination).hostname`
  when `_split` returns None, so a refused destination keys suppression on its real host.
- Assert the unusable-entry case BY CONSEQUENCE (admits nothing), not by log line.
- New tests: tests/test_oauth/redirect_dot_segments.py + one in tests/test_auth/handoff.py.
- CHANGELOG claim scoped to a *supplied* dot-segment redirect_uri/entry; note the origin-fallback
  branch is unchanged (Security #1109) and that `..%2f`/`%252e` stay admitted.
- No oauth.py change; no new incident site (that is #1098).

## Verification
Builder runs its OWN new regression tests targeted (fail-at-HEAD, pass-after) only.
The orchestrator owns the single closing suite run. No `--full`.
